CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct verb form: By the time the train arrived, we ____ for an hour.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The past perfect continuous describes an action continuing up to a past point.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: If she ____ earlier, she would have caught the bus.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The committee ____ its final report yesterday.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A completed action at a definite past time takes the simple past.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: This time tomorrow, I ____ my English examination.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The future continuous describes an action in progress at a future time.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Neither of the answers ____ correct.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Neither” is singular in this construction and takes “is”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The students ____ their project before the teacher entered.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Water ____ at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: General facts are expressed in the simple present.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: I ____ her since we were children.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Since” with a continuing state commonly takes the present perfect.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The auditorium ____ before the guests arrived.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The past perfect passive shows a completed action before another past event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: When I called, he ____ dinner.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a past moment.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: You ____ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle; it is a legal safety requirement.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Must” expresses strong obligation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: You ____ have informed us earlier; we could have helped.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Should have” expresses a past action that was advisable but did not happen.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: It ____ rain later, so carry an umbrella.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Might” expresses possibility.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Candidates ____ bring their admit cards into the examination hall.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Must” expresses a requirement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: She ____ speak three languages when she was ten.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Could” expresses past ability.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct passive form: The team completed the project.
options: The project was completed by the team.
The team was completed by the project.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Simple past active becomes “was/were + past participle” in the passive.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct passive form: They are repairing the bridge.
options: The bridge is repaired by them.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Present continuous passive uses “is/are being + past participle”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct passive form: Someone has stolen my bicycle.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Present perfect passive uses “has/have been + past participle”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct passive form: The school will announce the results tomorrow.
options: The school will be announced by results.
The results will be announced tomorrow.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Future passive uses “will be + past participle”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct reported form: Riya said, “I am tired.”
options: Riya said that she is tiring.
Riya said that she was tired.
Riya said that I am tired.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: In standard backshift, “am” changes to “was” and “I” to “she”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The teacher said to the class, “Do not waste time.”
options: The teacher told that not waste time.
The teacher advised the class not to waste time.
The teacher said the class do not waste time.
The teacher asked the class did not waste time.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Negative commands are commonly reported with “told/advised + object + not to”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: He asked me, “Where do you live?”
options: He asked me where I live?.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked where do I live.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Reported questions use statement word order and usually backshift the tense.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Maya said, “I have finished my work.”
options: Maya said that she finishes her work.
Maya said that she had finished her work.
Maya says that I finished my work.
Maya said she has finish her work.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Present perfect generally shifts to past perfect in reported speech.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Identify the subordinate clause: “Although it was raining, the match continued.”
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Although it was raining” is a concessive subordinate clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the sentence containing a relative clause.
options: The book that you lent me is fascinating.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “That you lent me” modifies the noun “book”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Complete the sentence: This is the place ____ we first met.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Where” introduces a relative clause referring to a place.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct connector: He worked hard, ____ he did not pass.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Yet” contrasts the effort with the unexpected result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct connector: Take an umbrella ____ it rains.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “In case” expresses precaution against a possible event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct simple sentence equivalent: “As he was ill, he stayed home.”
options: Although ill, but he stayed home.
He was ill and he stayed home because.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The participial phrase “Being ill” reduces the subordinate clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct complex form: “In spite of his poverty, he was honest.”
options: Though he was poor, he was honest.
Despite he was poor, he honest.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Though” introduces a concessive subordinate clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct compound sentence: “Despite the rain, they played.”
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A compound sentence joins independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct exclamatory form: “It is a very beautiful painting.”
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “How + adjective + subject + verb” forms an exclamation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Each of the players ____ given a certificate.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Each” is singular and takes “was”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The news ____ encouraging.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “News” is grammatically singular.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: A pair of shoes ____ missing.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The subject is the singular phrase “a pair”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The principal, along with the teachers, ____ attending the meeting.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The main subject “principal” is singular; the intervening phrase does not change agreement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Neither the manager nor the employees ____ available.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: With “neither…nor”, the verb commonly agrees with the nearer subject, “employees”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: There is ____ milk left; we can make one cup of tea.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Milk” is uncountable, so “a little” is appropriate.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Only ____ students understood the difficult question, but at least some did.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “A few” means some; “few” often suggests almost none.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: She is ____ honest person.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Honest” begins with a vowel sound, so “an” is used.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The meeting will begin ____ 10 a.m.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Use “at” with a precise clock time.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The library is closed ____ Sundays.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Use “on” with days of the week.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: He has been preparing ____ the examination for weeks.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard collocation is “prepare for an examination”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: She is interested ____ environmental science.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The correct collocation is “interested in”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: In “The committee reached a unanimous decision,” “unanimous” means:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A unanimous decision is one supported by all members.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The word “mitigate” most nearly means:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: To mitigate is to reduce the severity or impact of something.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: A “credible” source is one that is:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Credible means worthy of belief or trust.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: In “The plan was feasible,” “feasible” means:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Feasible means capable of being done successfully.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: A “concise” explanation is:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Concise writing expresses the main point briefly and clearly.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: To “scrutinise” a document is to:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Scrutinise means to inspect closely.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: An “ambiguous” statement is one that is:
options: open to more than one interpretation
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Ambiguous language can be understood in multiple ways.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: “Resilient” most nearly means:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Resilience is the ability to recover or adapt after setbacks.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: A “pragmatic” solution is:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Pragmatic describes an approach focused on practical results.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: “Inevitable” means:
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Inevitable means unavoidable or certain to occur.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: By next June, she ____ her degree.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The future perfect describes completion before a future point.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: At 8 p.m. yesterday, the volunteers ____ food parcels.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a specified past time.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: I wish I ____ more time to revise.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Wish” about a present unreal situation commonly takes the past form.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: If water reaches 100°C at standard pressure, it ____.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The zero conditional uses the simple present for general truths.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The speaker ____ for ten minutes when the microphone failed.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Past perfect continuous highlights duration before a past interruption.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The documents ____ by the time the officer arrived.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Past perfect passive marks completion before another past event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: She usually ____ the bus, but today she is walking.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A habitual action uses the simple present.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: The children ____ quietly when the lights went out.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The past continuous shows an ongoing action interrupted by another event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: I ____ this novel twice, so I know the ending.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Present perfect describes experience up to now.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: When we reached the station, the train ____.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The earlier past action takes past perfect.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “meticulous”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Meticulous means very careful and attentive to detail.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “reluctant”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “eloquent”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Eloquent describes effective, persuasive expression.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “obsolete”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Obsolete means no longer in use or useful.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “diligent”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Diligent means showing careful and persistent effort.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “plausible”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Plausible means seeming reasonable or likely.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “benevolent”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Benevolent means kindly and charitable.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “profound”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Profound can mean deep in thought, feeling or significance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “alleviate”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Alleviate means to make a problem or pain less severe.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “impartial”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Impartial means not favouring one side unfairly.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “contemplate”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Contemplate means to consider thoughtfully.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “versatile”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Versatile means able to adapt or perform varied functions.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “arduous”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Arduous describes something requiring great effort.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “deteriorate”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Deteriorate means to decline in condition.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “novel” as an adjective.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: As an adjective, novel means new or original.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “lucid”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Lucid writing or thought is clear.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “abundant”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Abundant means available in large quantities.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “frugal”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Frugal describes careful use of money or resources.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “vigilant”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Vigilant means alert to possible danger or difficulty.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the closest synonym of “endorse”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Endorse means publicly support or approve.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “scarce”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Abundant is the opposite of scarce.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “transparent”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Opaque means not allowing light through or not transparent.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “expand”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Contract means become smaller or reduce in size.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “optimistic”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Pessimistic expresses an expectation of negative outcomes.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “temporary”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Permanent means lasting or intended to last indefinitely.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “rigid”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Flexible means able to bend or adapt.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “conceal”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Reveal means make known or visible.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “hostile”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Friendly is the opposite of hostile.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “complex”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Simple contrasts with complex.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “reluctant”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Willing means ready or prepared to act.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “artificial”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Natural is the opposite of artificial.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “frequent”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Rare means occurring infrequently.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “generous”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Stingy means unwilling to give or spend.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “advance” as a verb meaning move forward.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Retreat means move back.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “victory”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Defeat is the opposite of victory.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “rational”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Irrational means not based on reason.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “humble”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Arrogant describes excessive self-importance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “mandatory”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Optional means not compulsory.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “accurate”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Inaccurate means not correct or exact.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the opposite of “preserve”.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Destroy is the opposite of preserve.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a decision.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard collocation is “make a decision”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ attention.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard expression is “pay attention”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a responsibility.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: We commonly say “take responsibility”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ an effort.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard phrase is “make an effort”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ progress.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard collocation is “make progress”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a promise.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A promise is commonly “kept” or “broken”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a complaint.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Lodge a complaint” is a standard formal expression.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ an opportunity.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Seize an opportunity” means take advantage of it.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a mistake.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The usual expression is “make a mistake”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct collocation: ____ a conclusion.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Draw a conclusion” means reach an inference.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Which sentence uses “affect” correctly?
options: She bought an affect of flowers.
The affect was obvious in the report.
The heat may affect the crops.
The affect of the story was a book.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Affect” is commonly a verb meaning influence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Which sentence uses “effect” correctly?
options: They effect their lunch every day.
The new rule had a positive effect.
The rule will effect the students yesterday.
The effect to the meeting is walking.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Effect” is commonly a noun meaning result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The principal will ____ the award at assembly.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Present” is the verb meaning formally give.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: Please ____ the instructions carefully.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Follow” is the appropriate verb.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The witness gave a ____ account of the event.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Reliable” is an adjective modifying “account”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: Her argument was logically ____.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Consistent” is the adjective needed after “was”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The organisation hopes to ____ public awareness.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Raise awareness” is the correct expression.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: Prices may ____ if demand increases.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Rise” is intransitive and means increase.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The school will ____ a new policy next month.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Adopt” means take up or begin using.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: Students must ____ their approach to different tasks.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Adapt” means adjust to new conditions.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The two accounts ____ each other.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Complement” means complete or go well with.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: She received a ____ for her clear presentation.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: A compliment is an expression of praise.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The committee will ____ the proposal next week.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Review” means examine or assess.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The new schedule is ____ with the school’s timetable.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Compatible with” means able to exist or work together.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The data are not sufficient to ____ the claim.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Substantiate” means support with evidence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The speaker tried to ____ the audience with evidence.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Persuade” is the verb meaning convince.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The results were ____ with the original prediction.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Consistent with” is the correct adjective phrase.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The school introduced a ____ measure to reduce waste.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Practical” describes a useful, workable measure.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The instructions were clear and ____.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Unambiguous” means clear and not open to multiple interpretations.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Choose the correct word: The author’s tone is ____ rather than angry.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Critical” is the adjective describing the tone.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (singular agreement with 'neither'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Neither of the plans is suitable.
Neither of the plans are suitable.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Neither” is singular in this construction.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the uncountable noun 'information'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Information” is uncountable and normally takes a singular verb.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the adjective 'senior'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: She is more senior to than me.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Senior” takes “to”, not “than”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (duration continuing to the present): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: He has working here from five years.
He is working here since five years.
He has been working here for five years.
He works here since five years.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: Use present perfect continuous with “for” to express duration continuing to now.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the 'no sooner...than' structure): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: No sooner had we arrived than it began to rain.
No sooner we had arrived when it began to rain.
No sooner we arrived than it began raining yesterday.
No sooner had we arrived when it began to rain.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard structure is “No sooner had…than…”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the 'hardly...when' structure): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Hardly had the bell rung than the students left.
Hardly the bell had rung than the students left.
Hardly the bell rang when the students had left.
Hardly had the bell rung when the students left.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard structure is “Hardly had…when…”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (a hypothetical condition): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: If I am you, I would apologised.
If I were you, I would apologise.
If I was you, I will apologise.
If I were you, I will apologising.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The subjunctive “were” is used in this hypothetical expression.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (agreement with 'one of'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: One of my friends has moved to Delhi.
One of my friend have moved to Delhi.
One my friends has move to Delhi.
One of my friends have moved to Delhi.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The subject is singular “one”, so use “has”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the uncountable noun 'furniture'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The furniture in these rooms are new.
The furniture in these rooms is new.
A furniture in these rooms is new.
The furnitures in these rooms are new.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Furniture” is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the 'prefer...to' structure): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: She prefer reading to watch television.
She prefers reading to watching television.
She prefers reading than watching television.
She prefers to reading than watch television.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: The standard construction is “prefer X to Y”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the use of 'despite'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Despite being tired, he completed the task.
Despite of being tired, he completed the task.
Despite he was tired, he completed the task.
Although being tired, but he completed the task.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.why: “Despite” is followed by a noun or gerund phrase, not a full clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Vocab.q: Editing exercise (the phrase 'the reason for'): which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The reason of the delay was unclear.
The reason why for delay was unclear.
The reason for the delay was unclear.

He has promised never to enter a house
He wants to become a soldier
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: He worries that the misunderstanding may expose his identity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the rattrap metaphor suggest about human choices?
options: Money has no influence on behaviour
People can never escape any mistake
Temptation can trap people, but they may still change
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The metaphor warns about temptation while allowing for redemption.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does Rajkumar Shukla approach Gandhi?
options: To seek help for peasants exploited by indigo planters
To ask for a school textbook
To invite Gandhi to a sports event
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Shukla persistently seeks Gandhi’s help for Champaran peasants.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What system placed Champaran peasants under pressure?
options: A system requiring them to grow indigo on part of their land
A law requiring all crops to be exported
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The indigo arrangement burdened peasants and favoured planters.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Gandhi’s refusal to leave Champaran significant?
options: It shows he has forgotten the law
It ends the inquiry before it begins
It asserts moral resistance to an unjust order
It is an attempt to gain a private estate
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Gandhi accepts legal consequences rather than abandon the peasants.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Gandhi’s work in Champaran demonstrate about leadership?
options: Listening, investigation and organised non-violent action
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: He gathers facts and builds a disciplined response.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does the chapter describe improvements beyond the indigo dispute?
options: The inquiry concerned only railway schedules
The planters built a palace for Gandhi
Gandhi’s approach also addressed education and social conditions
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The work included broader social reform.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What was important about the peasants overcoming fear?
options: It helped them challenge exploitation collectively
It forced them to leave Champaran
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Collective confidence was a major outcome of the movement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which method best characterises Gandhi’s approach in the chapter?
options: Non-violent civil resistance supported by facts
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Gandhi uses truth, non-violence and public inquiry.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What broader lesson does “Indigo” offer?
options: Only wealthy people can seek justice
Ordinary people can gain agency through organised, principled action
Education and health are unrelated to community welfare
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter presents collective action and ethical leadership as empowering.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the title refer to in the chapter?
options: A recipe competition at a school
Pancake make-up used in the film studio
A bakery owned by the narrator
A poetry festival held in a village
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: “Pancake” refers to make-up used in the studio.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How is the Gemini Studios environment portrayed?
options: As a workplace with hierarchy, routines and comic observations
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The narrator describes the studio’s people and workplace culture.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is one effect of the narrator’s humour?
options: It turns the account into a scientific report
It exposes absurdities in the studio’s social world
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Humour reveals contradictions and eccentricities.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the office boy dissatisfied?
options: He feels his talent and ambitions have not been recognised
He has no interest in cinema
He has been promoted too quickly
He wants to stop all films from being made
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: His frustration comes from a perceived mismatch between ambition and role.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the visit of the English poet reveal about the studio staff?
options: Cultural and professional misunderstandings can arise
The studio stops making films permanently
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The event highlights a gap between the visitor and the audience.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which narrative style dominates the chapter?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter uses recollection, irony and humour.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the chapter suggest about workplace status?
options: It has no connection to ambition
It can shape how people see themselves and others
It is always based only on talent
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Rank and recognition influence several characters’ attitudes.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the chapter more than a description of cosmetics?
options: It teaches chemical formulas for make-up
It is a history of all world cinema
It uses studio life to comment on people and institutions
It gives instructions for cooking pancakes
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The make-up department becomes a starting point for broader social commentary.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why do some writers dislike interviews?
options: They prefer all answers to be anonymous
They may see them as intrusive or distorting
They believe questions are always too easy
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Some writers regard interviews as an invasion of privacy or control over their image.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the chapter suggest about the interview as a form?
options: It is never useful to readers
It can reveal information but also create tension
It replaces all other forms of writing
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter presents both the usefulness and controversy of interviews.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Umberto Eco an interesting interview subject?
options: He refuses to discuss any intellectual activity
He discusses his work habits and the relationship between scholarship and fiction
He claims never to read books
He is interviewed only about sports
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Eco reflects on his varied intellectual and creative work.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Eco’s idea of “empty spaces” in a day suggest?
options: Every minute must be scheduled by others
Small intervals can be used productively
Writing can happen only at night
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: He uses small periods of time for thought and work.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does the chapter present the public figure’s interview experience?
options: As entirely controlled by the audience
As a form of silent reading
As shaped by both the interviewer’s questions and the subject’s responses
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Interviews depend on questions, responses and presentation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which concern is associated with interviews in the opening discussion?
options: The loss of all written records
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Interview subjects may worry about being represented inaccurately.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What quality helps make an interview informative?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Focused questions and considered answers support meaningful information.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is a balanced conclusion about interviews?
options: They have no effect on public understanding
They can be valuable while raising questions about privacy and representation
They are accurate in every circumstance
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter invites a nuanced view rather than a single extreme position.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is Sophie’s central tendency in the story?
options: She is uninterested in other people
She plans to become a farmer immediately
She imagines a glamorous future beyond her ordinary circumstances
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Sophie’s fantasies reflect her longing for a different life.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does Jansie differ from Sophie?
options: Jansie avoids all discussion of work
Jansie has already become a celebrity
Jansie is more practical about their likely future
Jansie shares every fantasy as fact
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Jansie recognises practical limits more readily.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Sophie fascinated by Danny Casey?
options: He represents glamour and escape from ordinary life
He offers her a job in a bakery
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The footballer becomes a focus for her imagination and hopes.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What role does Geoff play in Sophie’s imagination?
options: He is a trusted listener connected to a world she finds mysterious
He is the footballer Danny Casey
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Sophie confides in Geoff and imagines he understands her.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Sophie’s imagined encounter reveal?
options: The strength of her wishful thinking
Her ability to provide reliable evidence
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The encounter is tied to her fantasy and desire.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which theme is central to “Going Places”?
options: The tension between dreams and reality
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The story explores adolescent dreams and social realities.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why can Sophie’s fantasies be emotionally risky?
options: They may make ordinary reality disappointing
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Idealised expectations can deepen disappointment when unsupported by reality.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does the story portray adolescence?
options: As a period unrelated to social class
As a period of aspiration, identity-seeking and uncertainty
As a time when everyone has identical goals
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Sophie’s hopes reflect common adolescent tensions and constraints.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What emotion dominates the speaker’s response to her ageing mother?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem centres on awareness of ageing and possible loss.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does the poet notice the mother’s pale, wan face?
options: It makes her confront her mother’s frailty
It signals a change in the weather only
It proves the mother is pretending to sleep
It reminds her of a school prize
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The face prompts recognition of ageing and vulnerability.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the effect of the contrast with young trees and children?
options: It removes the poem’s emotional tension
It highlights vitality beside the mother’s ageing
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Images of movement and youth contrast with the mother’s stillness.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does the speaker smile at the end?
options: Because she has forgotten her mother
To conceal or manage her pain during farewell
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The smile masks anxiety and offers reassurance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which poetic device is central to the comparison of the mother’s face to a late winter’s moon?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The comparison uses “like” to connect the face with the moon.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the journey to the airport contribute to the poem?
options: It is a travel guide to airports
It creates a moment of parting and reflection
It resolves all fear of ageing
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The journey frames the emotional farewell.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: In “My Mother at Sixty-Six,” which theme is most prominent?
options: Ageing, mortality and a child’s love
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The speaker’s love is inseparable from fear of loss.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the poem’s language restrained rather than dramatic?
options: The poem is written as a news report
The quiet tone makes the speaker’s anxiety feel intimate and real
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Understatement and ordinary details intensify the emotion.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the poet ask people to do briefly?
options: Pause from activity and remain still
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem proposes a temporary pause for reflection.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Does the poem advocate permanent inactivity?
options: Yes; it rejects every human relationship
Yes; it demands that all work end forever
No; it asks people to increase conflict
No; it calls for a brief pause that may renew understanding
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The stillness is temporary and reflective, not a permanent rejection of life.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What might counting to twelve symbolise?
options: A list of twelve countries to conquer
A shared moment of pause and unity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The count offers a simple, common beginning for collective stillness.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How could silence help people, according to the poem?
options: It makes all problems disappear instantly
It may allow reflection on harmful habits and shared humanity
It removes the need for communication forever
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The pause encourages self-examination and a less destructive outlook.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What contrast does the poem draw between activity and stillness?
options: Both are described as exactly identical
Constant activity can conceal the need for reflection
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poet questions restless action and values reflective pauses.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which tone best fits the poem’s central appeal?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem gently urges readers to reconsider their behaviour.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the significance of “without rush, without engines” as an idea?
options: It describes a race between vehicles
It imagines a temporary break from mechanical, hurried life
It asks people to destroy every machine
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The image suggests release from speed and restless activity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What broad message can readers draw from the poem?
options: Nature has no relation to human behaviour
Silence alone solves every political problem
Self-awareness may help people live more peacefully with others and nature
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem links reflection with peace and awareness.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the poem suggest about beautiful things?
options: They are useful only as money
They offer lasting joy and comfort
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Beauty is presented as a continuing source of joy.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does the poet refer to the “flowery band” in a figurative sense?
options: It suggests a bond connecting people to life and beauty
It is a map of a river
It refers to a school uniform
It describes a prison chain literally
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The image conveys an emotional connection to the world.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does beauty help people face hardship?
options: It gives comfort and renews hope
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Beauty offers relief from sorrow and discouragement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which kinds of things contribute to the poem’s idea of beauty?
options: Natural forms and inspiring human stories
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem draws on nature and noble or inspiring experiences.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the effect of the poem’s imagery of shade and shelter?
options: It turns the poem into a weather report
It presents beauty as restorative and protective
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Shade and shelter convey relief and nourishment.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: In “A Thing of Beauty,” which theme is central to the poem?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem celebrates beauty’s lasting emotional influence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is beauty described as a source of joy over time?
options: It exists only for a few seconds
Its memory and presence can continue to sustain people
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem emphasises the continuing effects of beauty.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the overall tone of the poem?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem expresses faith in beauty’s sustaining power.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What do the roadside stand owners mainly hope to gain?
options: A government job in the city
Some income and a share in the prosperity passing them by
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: They hope travellers will buy their produce and improve their livelihood.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What contrast is central to the poem?
options: Rural poverty beside affluent passing traffic
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem contrasts the villagers’ needs with the wealth of travellers.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How do many passing motorists respond to the stand?
options: With indifference or irritation rather than helpful engagement
By asking the villagers to move into mansions
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The motorists often notice the stand as an inconvenience.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What criticism does the poem make of false promises of development?
options: They are unrelated to rural life
They may claim to help the poor while ignoring their real needs
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem questions development rhetoric that fails to address genuine needs.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the roadside stand symbolise?
options: Rural people’s desire for economic opportunity and dignity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The stand represents a small attempt to participate in the wider economy.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the speaker’s tone complex?
options: The speaker has no concern for anyone
Sympathy for the rural poor mixes with frustration and helplessness
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem conveys empathy but also anguish about persistent injustice.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the poem suggest about economic progress?
options: Its benefits may be unevenly distributed
It always reaches every village equally
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The rural community remains excluded from much of the prosperity around it.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which issue is most directly explored?
options: The discovery of a new planet
The history of a royal court
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem focuses on the gap between rural hardship and urban prosperity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What do Aunt Jennifer’s tigers represent?
options: A literal threat to the family
Confidence and freedom that contrast with her constrained life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The tigers appear bold and unafraid, unlike Aunt Jennifer.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the heavy wedding band suggest in the poem?
options: The burden of a restrictive marriage
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The ring symbolises the weight of marital and social constraints.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why are the tigers described as fearless?
options: They are afraid of the forest
They embody the freedom Aunt Jennifer lacks
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Their boldness contrasts with Aunt Jennifer’s anxiety.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What contrast shapes the poem?
options: The tigers’ energy versus Aunt Jennifer’s oppression
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem juxtaposes artistic freedom with a constrained personal life.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What role does embroidery play in the poem?
options: It becomes a medium through which Aunt Jennifer expresses imagination
It is a punishment assigned at school
It is a method of measuring time
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Her art gives expression to a freer imagined world.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the poem imply about art’s survival?
options: Art always disappears before the artist
Art has no relation to experience
The tigers may remain vibrant even after Aunt Jennifer’s suffering
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The embroidered figures endure as an expression of vitality.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: In “Aunt Jennifer’s Tigers,” which theme is central to the poem?
options: Gendered oppression and the desire for freedom
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The poem explores the burdens placed on women and their inner lives.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does the poem create contrast through imagery?
options: It pairs vigorous, confident animals with a fearful human figure
It describes every figure as equally timid
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The opposing images make the emotional conflict clear.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the third level at Grand Central symbolise for Charley?
options: Escape from the pressures of modern life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The third level offers Charley an imagined escape to a simpler past.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Galesburg attractive to Charley?
options: It is the busiest financial centre
He associates it with a peaceful, less hurried past
It offers him a modern airport
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Galesburg represents a calmer life away from contemporary stress.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does the story blend realism and fantasy?
options: It contains only a historical essay
An ordinary station setting leads to an unexplained time-slip experience
It gives a scientific proof of time travel
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The familiar station and impossible third level create ambiguity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Sam’s apparent disappearance add to the story?
options: It changes the story into a detective manual
It proves Charley never had a friend
It deepens the uncertainty about whether escape is fantasy or reality
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Sam’s experience leaves the boundary between reality and fantasy unclear.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What might the story suggest about escapism?
options: People may long to escape anxiety and complexity
The past was perfect in every way
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The story explores the desire to retreat from modern pressures.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the third level described as mysterious?
options: Its existence cannot be explained by ordinary logic
It is shown on every station map
It is a normal ticket counter
It is a clearly marked modern platform
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The third level appears to violate ordinary expectations.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the effect of the story’s ending?
options: It reveals the narrator is a machine
It gives a complete scientific explanation
It preserves ambiguity and invites interpretation
It ends with a court verdict
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The ending leaves readers uncertain about the events.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which genre feature is prominent in the story?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The impossible level reflects psychological longing through fantasy.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the king determined to kill tigers?
options: He wants to protect every tiger
A prophecy links his fate to a tiger
He is training as a forest guide
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The prophecy makes tiger hunting central to his obsession.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the king’s tiger hunt reveal about his character?
options: Pride and an attempt to control fate
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: His actions reveal arrogance and obsession with power.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does the story use satire?
options: It praises every royal decision without question
It exaggerates royal behaviour to criticise authority and vanity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The absurd hunt satirises rulers who misuse power.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the ending ironic?
options: The king becomes a wildlife scientist
The king’s fate is fulfilled through an unexpected, seemingly harmless object
The king decides never to hunt
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The wooden toy tiger causes the infection that leads to his death.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the toy tiger symbolise in the ending?
options: The irony of fate and the limits of human control
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The toy tiger becomes the instrument of the king’s downfall.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How do officials respond to the king’s obsession?
options: They all openly challenge him successfully
They often accommodate him to protect their own positions
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The officials act to preserve their positions under an authoritarian ruler.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: In “The Tiger King,” which theme is most prominent?
options: Power, arrogance and the unpredictability of fate
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The story satirises power and the illusion of control.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the effect of the story’s exaggerated tone?
options: It turns the narrative into a scientific paper
It makes the king’s actions realistic in every detail
It makes the criticism of royal vanity comic and sharp
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Exaggeration supports the story’s satirical effect.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Antarctica important to the narrator’s reflections?
options: It is the most densely populated continent
It has no connection to climate
It reveals clues about Earth’s past and environmental future
It contains every type of forest
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Antarctica offers evidence about climate and Earth’s history.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the journey help the students understand?
options: That climate change is impossible to study
That all continents have identical climates
The interconnectedness of ecosystems and human impact
That human actions never affect nature
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The trip highlights environmental connections and human responsibility.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the history of Gondwana relevant?
options: It describes a modern city council
It shows how continents and life have changed over geological time
It explains the invention of writing
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Gondwana helps explain continental history and the deep past.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is the significance of the small phytoplankton discussed in the chapter?
options: They are important to marine food webs and global systems
They are unrelated to ocean life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Phytoplankton play an important role in marine ecosystems and carbon cycling.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What warning does the chapter convey about climate change?
options: Small changes in connected systems can have wide consequences
Polar regions are isolated from the rest of Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter stresses interconnected environmental systems.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does the author emphasise Antarctica’s relative lack of human settlement?
options: It proves humans never influence the planet
It offers a stark setting to observe natural processes and environmental change
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The remote setting can make planetary processes easier to contemplate.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What role does scientific observation play in the journey?
options: It discourages students from asking questions
It connects direct experience with larger environmental questions
It replaces all evidence with imagination
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Observation helps students connect the landscape with science.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.topic: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which theme is central to the chapter?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The chapter encourages ecological awareness and responsibility.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is Dr Sadao conflicted when he finds the wounded American soldier?
options: He believes the man is a family member
He does not know how to treat wounds
His medical duty conflicts with wartime hostility and national loyalty
He wants to become a soldier
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Sadao must weigh professional ethics against national conflict.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Hana’s response to the wounded man reveal?
options: A desire to become a spy
Compassion despite fear and social pressure
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Hana assists despite anxiety and possible consequences.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does Sadao operate on the soldier?
options: He is ordered by the soldier’s commander
His responsibility as a doctor compels him to save a life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Medical ethics and humanity guide Sadao’s decision.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How do the servants respond to the presence of the American?
options: They are fearful and unwilling to accept the situation
They demand to join the army
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Their reaction reflects wartime prejudice and fear of consequences.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the General’s response reveal?
options: He is fully committed to protecting the soldier
He does not know that war exists
Self-interest can override consistent moral or official duty
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The General’s promises and inaction reveal self-serving behaviour.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does Sadao eventually help the soldier escape?
options: He seeks to resolve the danger while preserving the man’s life
He believes the soldier is not wounded
He wants the soldier to attack Japan
He has been paid by the soldier
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: He arranges an escape rather than allow the man to be captured or killed.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Which theme is central to “The Enemy”?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The story tests compassion against wartime divisions.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the title “The Enemy” invite readers to question?
options: Whether war has any historical dates
Whether an enemy label cancels a person’s humanity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The title challenges the moral consequences of defining people only as enemies.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does Derry initially avoid people?
options: He wants to become a doctor immediately
He expects others to judge him because of his scarred face
He has been forbidden to leave school
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Derry anticipates rejection and is defensive about his appearance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does Mr Lamb differ from Derry’s usual expectations of adults?
options: He tells Derry to hide indoors
He mocks every person he meets
He treats Derry with openness and encourages him to engage with life
He refuses to speak to Derry
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Mr Lamb challenges Derry’s assumptions through acceptance and conversation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the garden symbolise in the play?
options: A prison that must never be entered
A place where no living thing grows
A space for openness, growth and contact with the world
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The garden reflects Mr Lamb’s welcoming outlook.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the title “On the Face of It” meaningful?
options: It means that all first impressions are correct
It points to appearances and the danger of judging by them
It refers only to a map
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The title challenges superficial judgments based on appearance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Mr Lamb encourage Derry to do?
options: Live fully instead of allowing fear of others to control him
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Mr Lamb urges Derry to participate in life and look beyond stigma.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why does Derry’s mother worry about him?
options: She fears how others may treat him and tries to protect him
She wants him to leave home permanently
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Her concern reflects protective love, though it can also limit Derry.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is a central conflict in the play?
options: Derry’s isolation versus the possibility of connection
A dispute over money in a bank
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Derry struggles between self-protection and human connection.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the ending underline?
options: The importance of taking risks to build meaningful connections
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Derry’s return shows the impact of Mr Lamb’s encouragement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What connects the two autobiographical accounts in the chapter?
options: Experiences of discrimination and resistance to humiliation
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Both accounts show people confronting discriminatory treatment.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is the cutting of Zitkala-Sa’s hair distressing to her?
options: She is preparing for a wedding
Her hair carries cultural significance and the cutting is imposed on her
She wants to enter a beauty contest
She has asked for a new hairstyle
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The imposed haircut represents the suppression of cultural identity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does Bama’s childhood experience reveal about caste discrimination?
options: Discrimination exists only in written laws
Social prejudice can be embedded in everyday practices
Caste has no effect on daily life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Bama observes caste-based humiliation in an ordinary public scene.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: How does Bama respond to her brother’s advice?
options: She leaves her community without reflection
She channels her anger into education and achievement
She agrees that discrimination is fair
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Her brother advises education as a way to gain dignity and challenge injustice.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What is a shared theme in the two accounts?
options: The struggle to preserve dignity against oppressive social systems
The discovery of a new planet
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Both narrators resist systems that deny equal dignity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: Why is first-person narration effective in this chapter?
options: It proves every event is fictional
It turns the text into an impersonal list
It removes the experience of the narrator
It presents discrimination through personal memory and emotion
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Personal narration conveys the lived impact of discrimination.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What role does education play in the chapter’s message?
options: It always removes every form of prejudice immediately
It can help individuals challenge injustice and gain agency
It is available only to adults
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: Education is shown as a resource for resistance and empowerment.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.q: What does the chapter encourage readers to examine?
options: How to avoid all historical learning
How social norms can normalise unequal treatment
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literature.why: The accounts encourage critical reflection on prejudice and injustice.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which detail is essential in a formal school notice?
options: Name of issuing institution and date
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A notice needs clear institutional identification and date.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which style is most suitable for a notice about a lost water bottle?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Notices should communicate essential information efficiently.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A notice inviting students to register for a debate should clearly state:
options: Event, eligibility, deadline and contact details
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Readers need actionable event and registration details.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is least appropriate in a formal notice?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Ambiguous timing can prevent readers from acting correctly.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why should a notice use a heading?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A heading lets readers identify the notice’s subject at a glance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A formal invitation should usually maintain:
options: A courteous and appropriately formal tone
An informal chat style in every case
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Formal invitations use polite, conventional language.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which information is most important in an event invitation?
options: A list of all past events
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Invitees need the basic event details.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: In a formal reply declining an invitation, the writer should:
options: Thank the host and politely convey inability to attend
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A courteous decline acknowledges the invitation and states the response clearly.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which phrase is most suitable for a formal invitation?
options: You are cordially invited to attend
Hey, show up if you want
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: “Cordially invited” is appropriate formal phrasing.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the purpose of an RSVP request?
options: To ask for a book review
To ask invitees to confirm attendance
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: RSVP helps the host plan attendance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A letter to the editor should primarily:
options: Tell an unrelated personal story only
Present a public concern with evidence and constructive suggestions
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The purpose is to raise a public issue and advocate a reasoned response.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which opening is most suitable for a letter about unsafe roads?
options: I wish to draw attention to the growing safety concern on…
You will not believe this gossip…
I am writing about my favourite film…
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The opening should identify the public concern clearly.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is the strongest support for a claim about traffic congestion?
options: A rumour from an unknown source
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Evidence makes a public argument more credible.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What should the conclusion of a complaint letter to an editor do?
options: Request practical action or offer a clear recommendation
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A useful conclusion directs attention to possible action.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A job application should be tailored to:
options: Every job in exactly the same way
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Tailoring highlights relevant qualifications for the specific role.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which item belongs in a relevant résumé?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A résumé presents qualifications and experience relevant to the role.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why should a résumé use accurate dates and claims?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Accuracy protects credibility and supports verification.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A suitable article headline should:
options: Promise a result the article cannot support
Signal the topic clearly and attract relevant interest
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A headline should be concise and reflect the article’s focus.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is a useful structure for an analytical article?
options: Introduction, organised points with evidence, and conclusion
Only a headline and no body
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A logical structure helps readers follow the argument.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which feature makes an article analytical rather than merely descriptive?
options: It explains causes, effects and implications
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Analysis interprets information and explains relationships.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A report of a school event should generally include:
options: What happened, where, when, who was involved and key outcomes
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A report gives factual information about the event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which tone is best for a formal event report?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Reports should be clear, factual and restrained.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why is chronology useful in an event report?
options: It helps readers understand the sequence of events
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Chronological order makes the event easier to follow.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A speech opening is effective when it:
options: Addresses the audience and introduces the topic
Gives the conclusion before any context every time
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: An opening should engage listeners and establish the subject.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which feature helps a speech sound audience-aware?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Direct address and signposting support spoken communication.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A strong debate argument should include:
options: A clear claim supported by reasons and examples
A conclusion unrelated to the motion
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Reasoned support makes an argument persuasive.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the best way to respond to an opposing argument?
options: Address its reasoning with relevant counter-evidence
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A reasoned rebuttal engages with the argument itself.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which sentence is most concise?
options: The meeting, which is a meeting, begins at noon.
At the time when noon arrives, the meeting will begin.
The meeting is going to be beginning at the time of twelve noon.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The first sentence conveys the same information with fewer words.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which transition best introduces a contrast?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: “However” signals contrast.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which transition best introduces a consequence?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: “As a result” signals a consequence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: A paragraph is coherent when:
options: Its sentences connect logically around a central idea
It contains no transitions or relationships
Every sentence discusses a different topic
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Coherence depends on logical links and a clear focus.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the main purpose of proofreading?
options: To identify and correct errors before submission
To change every sentence into passive voice
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Proofreading checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and presentation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which source is best for supporting a factual claim in an article?
options: A credible source with relevant evidence
An anonymous message with no details
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Claims should be supported by reliable, relevant evidence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which phrase is most appropriate in a formal letter?
options: I would be grateful if you could consider…
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The phrase is courteous and formal.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why should a writer avoid unsupported absolute words such as “everyone” or “never”?
options: They can overstate a claim beyond the evidence
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Absolute claims need strong evidence and are often inaccurate.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the purpose of a concluding paragraph?
options: To add a new topic without transition
To synthesise the main point and leave a clear final impression
To repeat every sentence word for word
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A conclusion reinforces the argument or central message.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is an example of an objective report statement?
options: The programme was the greatest event ever.
The programme began at 10 a.m. and included three sessions.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The first sentence gives verifiable information without exaggerated judgement.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which approach best supports inclusive communication?
options: Use respectful terms and avoid stereotypes
Assume all readers share one experience
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Respectful, non-stereotyping language helps address a broad audience.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: When summarising a passage, a student should:
options: Add personal opinions not in the text
Retain main ideas and omit minor details
Focus only on the final word
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A summary condenses the central content in the student’s own words.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What does note-making primarily require?
options: Writing every point as a long paragraph
Organising key ideas using headings and concise points
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Notes select and organise important information efficiently.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why are abbreviations useful in notes when used carefully?
options: They remove the need to organise ideas
They make every note impossible to understand
They save space and time while preserving meaning
