CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Recognisable abbreviations can make notes more efficient.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What should a writer do when a source presents conflicting figures?
options: Check the sources, definitions and dates before drawing a conclusion
Ignore the difference and claim certainty
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Conflicting data should be investigated before making claims.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The survey; ended the results were analysed.
The survey ended the; results were analysed.
The survey ended; the results were analysed the next day.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A semicolon can join closely related independent clauses.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure?
options: The role requires to plan, organising and communicate.
The role requires planning, to organise and communication.
The role requires planning, organisation and to communicate.
The role requires planning, organising and communicating.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The first sentence uses consistent -ing forms in the series.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is the best revision of “Due to the fact that it rained, the match was cancelled”?
options: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.
The match was cancelled due to the fact of rain happening.
It rained, and the match was cancelled due to the fact that.
Due to rain being a fact, the match cancellation occurred.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: “Because” makes the sentence more concise without changing meaning.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the main purpose of an appropriate tone?
options: To use the longest possible words
To suit the audience, purpose and context
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Tone should match the communication situation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which practice helps avoid plagiarism?
options: Change only a few words and claim it as original
Credit sources and express borrowed ideas in your own words
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Acknowledging sources and paraphrasing responsibly avoids misrepresentation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is the most effective topic sentence?
options: Public transport can reduce congestion when it is reliable and accessible.
There are many things in the world.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The first sentence clearly states a focused claim.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why should paragraphs avoid overly long, unrelated sentences?
options: They can obscure relationships between ideas
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Overloaded sentences can make reasoning difficult to follow.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is the strongest evidence-based phrasing?
options: In the surveyed group, 62% preferred the revised schedule.
Nobody could disagree with the change.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The statement defines the group and gives a measurable result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What should an invitation reply include when accepting?
options: A clear acceptance and, where appropriate, thanks
A new event with no connection
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A reply should make attendance status clear and courteous.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which detail is most useful in a lost-and-found notice?
options: A long account of the finder’s childhood
The weather forecast for next month
A description of the item and how to contact the owner
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The description and contact route help reunite the item with its owner.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the main difference between a report and a personal diary entry?
options: There is no difference in purpose
A report is usually factual and audience-oriented; a diary is personal and reflective
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Reports communicate event information; diaries record personal experiences.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which revision best improves clarity?
options: Replace vague pronouns with the specific noun they refer to
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Specific references reduce ambiguity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What should a writer do if an article includes a chart?
options: Assume readers will interpret it identically
Explain what the relevant data show and avoid unsupported conclusions
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Charts need context and careful interpretation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which expression is a polite request?
options: Could you please provide the details by Friday?
You must know what I mean.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: The first phrase is courteous and specific.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is the purpose of a call to action in a public-awareness article?
options: To suggest a concrete next step for readers
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A call to action tells readers how they can respond.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which is the best way to make a long report easier to scan?
options: Remove all headings and paragraph breaks
Use informative headings and logically grouped sections
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Headings and grouping improve navigation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: When should a writer use quotation marks around a phrase?
options: When reproducing exact words from a source, with proper attribution
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Quotation marks indicate exact quoted wording; attribution is still needed.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Which feature most improves a formal email’s usability?
options: A specific subject line and clear purpose
A blank subject line and unclear request
Several unrelated topics in one paragraph
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A useful subject line and clear purpose help the recipient respond.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: Why should a report distinguish facts from opinions?
options: The distinction makes writing longer without benefit
Readers can judge the evidence and the writer’s interpretation separately
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: Separating facts and interpretations improves transparency.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.q: What is a good final check before submitting an answer?
options: Check relevance, structure, grammar and factual accuracy
Add a new argument at random
CBSE 12 - English Core - Creative Writin.why: A final review checks both content and expression.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Compare “The Last Lesson” and “Memories of Childhood”: what shared concern appears in both?
options: The effect of oppression on identity and dignity
The rules of a sports competition
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both texts show how oppressive systems threaten identity and dignity.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What connects “Lost Spring” and “Indigo” thematically?
options: People confronting social and economic exploitation
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both explore exploitation and the need for social change.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: How do “Deep Water” and “On the Face of It” portray personal growth?
options: Through confronting fear and changing limiting beliefs
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both characters move toward greater freedom by facing fears.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What do “The Rattrap” and “The Enemy” suggest about compassion?
options: It can challenge prejudice and influence moral choices
It has no impact on behaviour
It is a sign of weakness in every case
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Compassion influences the peddler’s change and Sadao’s medical decision.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a shared concern of “Going Places” and “The Third Level”?
options: The desire to escape ordinary pressures through imagination
The scientific study of marine life
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both texts explore forms of escape from everyday life.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: How do “A Roadside Stand” and “Lost Spring” draw attention to inequality?
options: They focus only on wealthy rulers
They show disadvantaged people excluded from wider prosperity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both depict social and economic marginalisation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a useful contrast between “A Thing of Beauty” and “Keeping Quiet”?
options: One is a report and the other a job application
Both argue that nature should be destroyed
One celebrates beauty as sustaining; the other urges reflective stillness
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The poems offer different routes to emotional and ethical renewal.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What do “Aunt Jennifer’s Tigers” and “The Last Lesson” have in common?
options: Both present a comic royal hunt
Both are about an Antarctic expedition
Both use a central image to express a larger struggle for freedom or identity
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The tigers and the language lesson become symbols of deeper struggles.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which pair most directly addresses the cost of prejudice?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Both works show how social or national divisions affect people.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which pair most directly explores the relationship between fear and courage?
options: “A Roadside Stand” and “A Thing of Beauty”
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Douglas confronts fear, while Sadao faces a moral dilemma under wartime pressure.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text uses satire to criticise the misuse of authority?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: “The Tiger King” uses comic exaggeration to criticise royal arrogance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which work most clearly questions whether appearances should determine how people are treated?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The play challenges judgments based on physical appearance.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text most directly explores the power of language as cultural identity?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The story links language with identity and cultural freedom.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which poem most directly presents art as an expression of a constrained inner life?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Aunt Jennifer’s embroidery expresses a freedom she does not experience in life.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text most directly asks readers to consider humanity beyond national identity?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Sadao’s choice challenges the idea that an enemy label removes human worth.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text centres on a young person’s hopes clashing with practical reality?
options: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Sophie’s fantasies contrast with her circumstances.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which work most directly examines the unequal distribution of economic opportunity?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The poem highlights rural poverty beside affluent traffic.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text focuses on the social value of education as resistance?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Bama’s story connects education with dignity and agency.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which text makes a journey into a setting for environmental reflection?
options: Journey to the End of the Earth
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The Antarctic journey prompts reflection on planetary systems.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Which chapter uses a studio setting to reveal workplace hierarchy and social behaviour?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The chapter observes status and personalities in a film studio.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a shared feature of “The Rattrap” and “The Last Lesson”?
options: A character’s understanding changes through an important experience
Both are narrated as statistical reports
Both centre on a king’s hunting vow
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: The peddler changes morally, while Franz recognises the value of language and learning.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What distinguishes a literary inference from a literal detail?
options: An inference draws a supported conclusion from clues
A literal detail always expresses a theme
An inference repeats a date exactly
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Inference combines textual clues to reach a reasonable conclusion.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Why should a literary interpretation be supported with textual evidence?
options: It guarantees every interpretation is identical
It makes the argument reasoned and defensible
It replaces the need to explain
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Evidence connects the interpretation to the work.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is dramatic irony?
options: A list of events in time order
A situation in which the audience knows something a character does not
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Dramatic irony depends on a gap between audience and character knowledge.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a symbol in literature?
options: A word with only a dictionary meaning
An object or image that suggests a larger meaning
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Symbols carry meaning beyond their literal presence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the purpose of a foil character?
options: To narrate every event in first person
To highlight traits of another character through contrast
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: A foil character makes another character’s qualities clearer by contrast.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a reliable way to identify a poem’s tone?
options: Consider diction, imagery and the speaker’s attitude
Count only the number of lines
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Tone emerges from word choice, imagery and attitude.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What does a motif do in a literary work?
options: Repeats an image or idea to develop meaning
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: A recurring motif reinforces themes or patterns.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the difference between theme and plot?
options: Theme is a central idea; plot is the sequence of events
Theme is always a character’s name
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Plot describes what happens; theme concerns the work’s central ideas.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is an unreliable narrator?
options: A narrator who only describes weather
A narrator who is always a poet
A narrator whose account may be incomplete or questionable
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: An unreliable narrator cannot be accepted uncritically.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What does juxtaposition achieve in a poem?
options: It places contrasting images or ideas together for effect
It makes every line a question
It replaces the poem with prose
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Juxtaposition invites readers to compare contrasting elements.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is an extended metaphor?
options: A rhyme at the end of a line
A metaphor developed across several lines or throughout a work
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: An extended metaphor sustains a comparison over a longer passage.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: Why might a writer use understatement?
options: To express an idea with restraint that can intensify its effect
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Understatement can make emotion or irony more powerful.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the function of setting in a story?
options: It gives only the author’s age
It has no connection to meaning
It shapes atmosphere and can influence characters and events
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Setting provides context and can affect mood and action.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a narrative flashback?
options: A prediction of a future event only
A change from prose to rhyme
A return to an earlier event within the story
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: A flashback interrupts the present narrative to show an earlier event.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What does a character’s internal conflict involve?
options: A battle between two armies only
A struggle between competing feelings, beliefs or choices
A conflict between two unrelated chapters
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Internal conflict occurs within a character.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the role of imagery in poetry?
options: It creates sensory impressions and helps convey ideas
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Imagery appeals to the senses and supports meaning.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is a rhetorical question?
options: A question asked only in a courtroom
A question asked for effect rather than to obtain a direct answer
A question that must be answered with a number
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Rhetorical questions emphasise a point or prompt reflection.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the effect of repetition in a poem?
options: It can emphasise an idea, create rhythm or reinforce emotion
It always indicates a printing error
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: Repetition can give prominence and structure to ideas.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is an allusion?
options: A change from past to present tense
An indirect reference to a known person, event, text or idea
A description of a sound only
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: An allusion relies on readers recognising a reference.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What does a first-person narrator commonly use?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: First-person narration presents events through an “I” or “we” voice.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.q: What is the purpose of a character arc?
options: To show how a character changes over the course of a work
To list the chapters by page number
CBSE 12 - English Core - Literary Analys.why: A character arc traces development or change.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct completion: If the school had announced the change earlier, more students ____ informed.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The third conditional uses “would have + past participle” for an unreal past result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct completion: If I had more time, I ____ another draft.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The second conditional uses past form in the if-clause and “would + base verb” in the result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct completion: Unless you revise carefully, you ____ avoid careless errors.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Unless” means “if not”; “may not” expresses a possible result.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the connector that best completes: The evidence was limited; ____, the team avoided a firm conclusion.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Therefore” introduces a consequence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the connector that best completes: ____ the first draft was clear, it needed stronger evidence.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Although” introduces a contrast between clarity and the need for evidence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the connector that best completes: The proposal was expensive. ____, it offered long-term savings.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Nevertheless” signals contrast.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the sentence with the modifier placed correctly.
options: Walking to school, Meera noticed the new library.
Walking to school, the new library was noticed by Meera.
The new library walking to school noticed Meera.
Meera noticed walking to school the new library was.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The opening phrase correctly modifies Meera, the person walking.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the sentence that avoids a dangling modifier.
options: After finishing the report, the figures were checked.
While reading the report, the conclusion was confusing.
Having finished the report, the deadline was met by Arjun.
After finishing the report, Arjun checked the figures.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Arjun is clearly the person who finished the report.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation.
options: The results were clear, however more research was needed.
The results were clear; however, more research was needed.
The results were clear however; more research was needed.
The results; were clear, however more research was needed.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: A semicolon can separate independent clauses joined by a conjunctive adverb.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: The students project’s were displayed in the hall.
The student’s projects were displayed in the hall. (meaning all students)
The students projects’ were displayed in the hall.
The students’ projects were displayed in the hall.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The plural possessive “students’” shows that the projects belong to multiple students.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Which sentence correctly uses a colon?
options: Bring three items a pen: an ID card and a notebook.
Bring three items: a pen, an ID card and a notebook.
Bring: three items a pen, an ID card and a notebook.
Bring three: items a pen, an ID card and a notebook.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: A colon can introduce a list after a complete clause.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure with consistent infinitive phrases?
options: The workshop teaches students plan, researching and to present.
The workshop teaches students to plan, research and presenting.
The workshop teaches students to plan, to research and to present.
The workshop teaches students planning, to research and presentation.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The three infinitive phrases are parallel.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure with consistent gerund forms?
options: She enjoys reading, writing and debating.
She enjoys read, write and debating.
She enjoys to read, writing and to debate.
She enjoys reading, to write and debates.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: All items in the series use gerunds.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct pronoun: Every applicant must bring ____ own identification.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Singular “they/their” is widely accepted for a person whose gender is unspecified.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct pronoun: The committee submitted ____ report on Friday.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Its” is the possessive determiner for the singular collective noun in this sentence.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct form: The speaker explained the issue with great ____.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The noun “clarity” follows “with great”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct form: The committee made a ____ assessment of the proposal.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: An adjective is needed to modify “assessment”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct form: The policy was implemented ____ across the district.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: An adverb modifies the verb “implemented”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct form: The student gave a ____ explanation of the chart.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: An adjective modifies the noun “explanation”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct reported form: “Are you ready?” the coach asked me.
options: The coach asked me whether I was ready.
The coach said that are you ready.
The coach asked me was I ready.
The coach asked whether was I ready.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Reported yes/no questions use “whether/if” and statement word order.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct reported form: “Please submit the form today,” the clerk said.
options: The clerk requested me to submit the form that day.
The clerk said please submit the form today.
The clerk asked me submit the form today.
The clerk requested that I submitted the form yesterday.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: A polite request can be reported with “requested + object + to-infinitive”; “today” may shift to “that day”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct passive form: People speak English in many countries.
options: English was speak in many countries.
English is spoken in many countries.
People are spoken English in many countries.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Simple present passive uses “is/are + past participle”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct passive form: The staff had prepared the room.
options: The room had been prepared by the staff.
The room was prepare by the staff.
The room has prepared by the staff.
The staff had been prepared the room.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Past perfect passive uses “had been + past participle”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct article: She hopes to study at ____ university in Delhi.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “University” begins with the consonant /juː/ sound, so “a” is used.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct article: It was ____ honour to meet the author.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Honour” begins with a vowel sound, so “an” is used.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct preposition: The final decision depends ____ the evidence.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The standard expression is “depend on”.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct preposition: The school is committed ____ reducing waste.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: “Committed to” is followed by a noun or gerund.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Choose the correct preposition: She apologised ____ the delay.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The standard expression is “apologise for” something.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: When a poem contrasts a bright image with a dark one, what should a reader examine first?
options: Whether the poem contains a dialogue
Whether the images have the same number of letters
How the contrast develops the poem’s meaning or tone
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Contrasting imagery often develops theme, mood or conflict.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Why might an author leave a story’s ending unresolved?
options: To make the plot a dictionary entry
To invite readers to consider multiple plausible interpretations
To prove the story has no meaning
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: An open ending can encourage reflection and interpretation.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What is a theme statement expected to express?
options: Only the name of the main character
A general insight about human experience developed by the work
The page number of a chapter
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: A theme statement expresses an idea the work explores, not just its topic.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: How does irony differ from a straightforward statement?
options: It involves a meaningful gap between expectation and reality or intended meaning
It means every word is literal
It always uses a question mark
It can occur only in poetry
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Irony depends on a contrast between appearance, expectation and reality.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Which question best supports analysis of a character’s motivation?
options: How many letters are in the character’s name?
What colour is the book cover?
How many pages are in the edition?
What evidence shows why the character makes this choice?
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Motivation analysis links choices to evidence and context.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What is the best approach when two readers interpret a poem differently?
options: Compare their interpretations against details in the poem
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Interpretations should be evaluated through textual support.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What is a narrative point of view?
options: The perspective from which events are presented
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Point of view describes the narrative perspective.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What does a recurring object often do in a story?
options: Gain symbolic significance through repeated appearances
Guarantee that the plot never changes
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Repeated objects can develop meaning as symbols or motifs.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Why should readers consider historical context when studying a text?
options: It can clarify the social conditions and assumptions shaping the work
It always gives one unquestionable interpretation
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Context helps explain a work’s circumstances but does not replace textual analysis.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What makes a comparison between two texts convincing?
options: A list of titles with no explanation
A clear point of comparison supported by specific evidence from both
A claim based only on personal preference
A summary of only one text
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Strong comparison uses a shared criterion and evidence from both works.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: Which is the strongest analytical claim about a character?
options: The character’s repeated choices reveal growing awareness of responsibility.
The chapter is printed in black ink.
The character is present in chapter three.
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: The first statement interprets a pattern of choices and development.

CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.q: What does an alliterative phrase repeat?
options: The same plot event in every chapter
Only vowel letters at the ends of lines
Initial consonant sounds in nearby words
CBSE 12 - English Core - Grammar & Liter.why: Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds.
